existing.description: The Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship programme awards 18 full scholarships each academic year, including a tuition fee waiver and a monthly stipend, to highly talented students from outside the EU who have been admitted to a Maastricht University master's programme. It combines the High Potential Scholarship, funded by the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund, with the ministry-funded NL Scholarship. For the 2027-2028 intake, scholarship applications run from 1 October 2026 to 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET), the participating master's application must be complete through Studielink before 10 December 2026, and applicants must be non-EU/EEA (also excluding Switzerland and Surinam), aged 35 or under on 1 September 2027, with a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 and no previous degree-seeking study in the Netherlands. Recipients receive a living-expense stipend of EUR 20,150 over 13 months or EUR 38,750 over 25 months, tuition fees, visa costs and EUR 700 of health and liability insurance paid at cost, a mandatory UM room until 16 July 2028 and a two-week Pre-Academic Training programme. Only about 2% of applicants are awarded.
eligibility: Hold a nationality from outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland or Surinam and meet the requirements for a Dutch entry visa and residence permit
Not have dual nationality from an EU/EEA country or Switzerland
Have applied for admission to a participating full-time master's programme for 2027-2028 and submitted the application file in full, meeting all admission requirements, before 10 December 2026
Meet the specific admission requirements of the chosen UM master's programme
Never have participated in a degree-seeking higher education programme in the Netherlands (completed exchange programmes are welcome)
Preference is given to candidates who have not yet obtained a master's degree
Be 35 years of age or younger on 1 September 2027
Have excellent results in prior education, with a GPA of 7.5 out of 10 or higher (at least 75%, or 3 out of 4)
Agree to act as a UM NL High Potential and UM ambassador during and after studies by sharing experience in at least one information session
Submit only one application, for one UM scholarship only
existing.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA, non-Swiss, non-Surinam applicants admitted to a participating full-time Maastricht University master's programme for 2027-2028, with a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10, aged 35 or under on 1 September 2027, who have never studied in a Dutch degree programme.
benefits: Two-week mandatory Pre-Academic Training starting the first week of August 2027
coverage: Living-expense stipend of EUR 1,550 per month, EUR 20,150 for 13 months or EUR 38,750 for 25 months
Tuition fees paid at cost by the UM International Services Desk
Visa application costs paid at cost
Health and liability insurance of EUR 700
Pre-Academic Training costs and the International Student Ambassador Programme (first block) paid at cost
A mandatory UM room allocated until 16 July 2028
Not covered: air tickets and the cleaning fee of about EUR 75
requirements: Apply for a participating master's programme via Studielink and complete the file by 10 December 2026
Pay any handling fee the programme requires by 10 December 2026, which the scholarship does not cover
Receive a UM student ID number to access the scholarship application form
Complete all registration requirements by the scholarship deadline of 1 February 2027, except legal residence, tuition payment and the hard copy of the diploma
Upload all documents in .doc, .docx or PDF format; documents cannot be added or replaced after submission
documents: Curriculum vitae of maximum two A4 pages, mentioning awards or prizes
Letter of motivation using the UM template
Official university transcript showing a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10
Reference letter dated no earlier than February 2026, following the UM guidelines, written by a (former) professor, lecturer or employer and uploaded by the applicant
Contact details of one referee including the relationship, work telephone number with country code and work or institutional email address
existing.english_requirement: Not specified on the scholarship page; the chosen master's programme sets its own English language requirements.
application_method: Apply for a participating master's programme through Studielink
Log in to the UM scholarship application form with your UM account once you have your student ID
Complete the UM motivation letter template
Upload the CV, proof of academic excellence, financial needs statement, reference letter and referee details
Submit before 1 February 2027, 23:59 CET, and sign and return the award letter if selected
existing.selection_notes: The UM International Services Desk checks completeness after 1 February, forwards complete files to each faculty in February 2027, each faculty ranks its top five, the shortlist is confirmed by the end of March, shortlisted candidates are invited to an online interview, and statuses (selected, waitlisted or rejected) are communicated in April 2027, final by May 2027. Maastricht states that only about 2% of applicants receive the scholarship.
existing.best_fit: High-achieving non-EU/EEA applicants with a GPA of 7.5 or higher who can satisfy the GPA, age and ambassador requirements and who need full funding including tuition, and who are willing to accept the mandatory room and Pre-Academic Training.
existing.notes: The programme combines the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund's High Potential Scholarship with the ministry-funded NL Scholarship, so it covers substantially more than the NL Scholarship alone. Handling fees for programmes that charge one are not covered. The application portal is unavailable between 22 and 26 October because of an upgrade. Applicants can submit only one UM scholarship application; multiple applications are disqualified.
existing.duration: If the scholarship covers only tuition fees, make sure you can finance your living expenses (rent, food and insurances) for the complete duration of your studies.
existing.application_period: One round per academic year for the September 2027 intake: scholarship applications open 1 October 2026, the master's application must be complete by 10 December 2026, scholarship applications close 1 February 2027 23:59 CET, statuses are given in April 2027 and final results by May 2027.
existing.deadline_display: "Applications are open from 1 October 2026 until 1 February 2027 23:59 CET." The participating master's programme application must be complete through Studielink "before 10 December 2026".
existing.program_type: University full scholarship (university fund + national NL Scholarship)

existing.description: The University of Twente Scholarship is a scholarship for excellent students from non-EU/EEA countries applying for an English-taught master's programme at the University of Twente. Its value ranges from EUR 3,000 to EUR 22,000 for one year and is intended as compensation for study-related costs, with no costs such as tuition fees paid on the student's behalf; for two-year programmes a second-year award of an equal amount is possible if the student obtains an average grade of 7 out of 10 and at least 50 percent of the European Credits at the end of the third quartile of the first year. Applicants must first obtain an academic admission letter for a qualifying 2027/2028 master's programme, hold a UT student number, meet English requirements of IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 90 with 6.0 in speaking, not be eligible for a Dutch study loan, and belong to the top 5 to 10 percent of their graduating class. The application form opens on 15 October 2026 and closes on 1 April 2027 at 16:00 CET, with results in the first week of May 2027.
eligibility: Have applied for admission to a qualifying UT master's programme and already hold an academic (possibly conditional) admission letter
Be (provisionally) admitted to a qualifying UT master's programme starting in the academic year 2027/2028 (September)
Have a UT student number
Not have graduated from a UT undergraduate or graduate programme
Comply with Dutch entry visa conditions where applicable
Meet the general English test requirement: academic IELTS 6.5 (or TOEFL iBT 90) plus 6.0 (TOEFL iBT 20) in the speaking subscore
Not be eligible for a Dutch study loan
Belong to the best 5 to 10 percent of the graduating class at the home university
Not pay the statutory tuition fee, including non-EU/EEA students whose Dutch residence permit entitles them to it
Not be a Dutch or current UT student, and not an EU/EEA national
existing.eligibility_summary: Excellent students from non-EU/EEA countries who have been provisionally admitted to a qualifying University of Twente English-taught master's programme starting in the 2027/2028 academic year, are not eligible for a Dutch study loan, do not pay the statutory tuition fee and belong to the top 5 to 10 percent of their graduating class.
benefits: One-off UTS of EUR 3,000 to EUR 22,000
Possible additional UTS of an equal amount for the second year of a two-year programme
Access to further UT scholarships such as the Kipaji Scholarship, which requires a UTS application
coverage: Cash compensation for study-related costs of EUR 3,000 to EUR 22,000 for one year
Possible equal second-year award for two-year master's programmes, conditional on progress
No tuition fees paid on the student's behalf
The student decides how to spend the money
requirements: Apply for the master's programme first and obtain an academic admission letter
Wait for the application form to open on 15 October 2026, 09:00 CET
Apply for the scholarship with your UT student number
existing.english_requirement: Academic IELTS 6.5 (or TOEFL iBT 90) plus 6.0 (TOEFL iBT 20) in the speaking subscore.
application_method: Apply for a qualifying UT master's programme and receive a (conditional) admission letter
Use your student number to complete the online UTS application form when it opens on 15 October 2026
Submit the application before the 1 April 2027, 16:00 CET deadline
existing.selection_notes: The University of Twente defines eligibility as excellence: applicants must belong to the best 5 to 10 percent of their graduating class at their home university. Results are announced in the first week of May 2027, and only one UT scholarship can be awarded per student.
existing.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants with a top-decile academic record who already hold a conditional admission to an eligible UT master's programme and who can cover tuition and the remaining living costs themselves.
existing.notes: The UTS is not available for the Faculty of Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation (ITC), for the pre-Master programme, for Dutch or current UT students, for EU/EEA students or for students paying the statutory tuition fee. Pre-Master students who continue into a master's programme may not apply either. Applicants can be awarded only one UT scholarship, and the Kipaji Scholarship can only be requested by applying for the UTS.
existing.application_period: Annual round for the September 2027 intake: the application form opens on 15 October 2026 and closes on 1 April 2027 at 16:00 CET; results in the first week of May 2027.
existing.deadline_display: "Application form opens per 15 October 2026, 09.00 CET" and "Application forms closes per 1 April 2027, 16.00 CET (for programmes starting September 2027)". Results are announced in the first week of May 2027.
existing.program_type: University scholarship for excellent non-EU/EEA students applying to an English-taught master's programme
